considered_statement: GD is typically subdivided into three types, with type 1 (GD1) being most common and having the least severe manifestations.
exclusion_reason: the only retrievable OA disease-level severity framing for Gaucher disease type 1 (C1961835) places it as the LEAST severe of the three GD types ('type 1 (GD1) being most common and having the least severe manifestations'); although the frozen R3 severity function pattern-matches 'severe' inside 'least severe' to tier 0.75, the statement is COMPARATIVE -- it characterises GD1 as the mild, non-neuronopathic end of the GD spectrum relative to the neuronopathic types 2/3 -- not a clean disease-level severe magnitude for GD1's own dominant untreated sequela; S left [H], not lifted

considered_statement: Background Gaucher disease (GD) in children is highly heterogeneous, severe, and particularly devastating in GD type 3 (GD3), which has systemic and neurological involvement.
exclusion_reason: the retrievable OA 'devastating' severity magnitude is explicitly attributed to GD TYPE 3 ('highly heterogeneous, severe, and particularly devastating in GD type 3 (GD3)'), the neuronopathic form, not to the Gaucher disease umbrella entity's (C0017205) own dominant untreated sequela; although the frozen R3 severity function maps 'devastating' to tier 1.0 and the heterogeneity wording does not trip the spectrum_S override, the magnitude is COMPARATIVE (it singles out GD3) and the umbrella spans non-neuronopathic-to-neuronopathic forms, so a clean disease-level umbrella severity tier is not defensibly isolable; S left [H], not lifted
